title: Identity provisioning matrix + SAML onboarding review with Nova Energy
summary: Redwood and Nova Energy walked through SAML SSO onboarding, SCIM provisioning patterns, RBAC least-privilege matrix, audit log retention and KMS options. Customer emphasized EU data residency, strict role separation for ops vs platform, and auditability for SOC 2/ISO. Agreed next steps: share SCIM mapping template, SOC2 report, and schedule a pilot SSO test in staging.
next_steps: Redwood to send SCIM group mapping template and example payload (Emily) by 2025-11-18
Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II and ISO certificate PDFs (Marco) by 2025-11-17
Customer to provision a staging SP and provide metadata URL (Aisha) by 2025-11-22
Schedule 60m pilot SSO test with SRE and Platform (Emily + Jared) week of 2025-11-24
action_items: Emily Carter | Send SCIM mapping template + example JSON | 2025-11-18
Marco Singh | Share SOC2/ISO artifacts and security whitepaper | 2025-11-17
Aisha Khan | Provide SAML metadata URL and test user accounts | 2025-11-22
Jared Lin | Stand up staging SP and enable debug logs | 2025-11-20
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Attendees: Emily Carter (Redwood AE), Marco Singh (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood Solutions), Aisha Khan (Nova IT Security), Tom Reyes (Nova Platform), Priya Patel (Nova Compliance), Jared Lin (Nova SRE)

[00:00] Emily Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can you hear me?
[00:05] Aisha Khan: Yep, loud and clear, thanks.
[00:08] Marco Singh: Hi, thanks. I'll jump straight into the technical bits once we cover goals.
[00:15] Emily Carter: Goal for today is to align on SAML SSO flow, SCIM provisioning patterns, and the RBAC least-privilege matrix. Also to cover audit log retention and encryption options for Nova's EU workloads.
[00:30] Tom Reyes: For context, we run most production in eu-west-1 and any PII must stay in EU. We also have strict separation between platform engineers and operators — they can't elevate without change requests.
[00:45] Marco Singh: Makes sense. On SSO we support SAML 2.0 SP, and we can do both metadata file upload and metadata URL fetch. Do you have an IdP today?
[00:55] Aisha Khan: We use Okta for enterprise, but some teams provision some apps via SCIM and others via manual mapping. Our ask is to avoid wide group-to-role mappings; we'd like least-privilege by default.
[01:10] Emily Carter: Totally — that's what our RBAC templates are for. We usually recommend a small set of base roles: viewer, editor, admin, and then specialized roles for billing and security with scoped permissions.
[01:25] Priya Patel: For compliance, we need audit trails tied to SAML assertions and SCIM changes. SOC 2 auditors want user lifecycle proof and ability to show who provisioned accounts.
[01:40] Marco Singh: We capture SAML SSO events, SCIM provisioning events, and detailed audit logs with actor, action, target, timestamp. By default retention for audit logs is 90 days on hosted, but we can extend to 2 years as an add-on or push to your own SIEM via webhook/CloudTrail export.
[01:55] Jared Lin: Are logs tamper-evident? We need chain of custody for some workflows.
[02:02] Marco Singh: Good question — we provide signed log export and can integrate with your KMS to envelope-encrypt exports. We also support writing to an append-only store in your account for stronger guarantees.
[02:20] Tom Reyes: On SCIM, we want group->role mapping where only specific groups map to privileged roles and scoping by org unit. Does Redwood support attribute-based rules?
[02:35] Marco Singh: Yes, we support SCIM group mappings plus attribute-based conditions — you can map groups to roles and add filters like department=="platform". We will send an example mapping JSON.
[02:50] Aisha Khan: One concern: Just-in-Time provisioning vs. pre-provisioning. For security we prefer pre-provisioning to control access, but for dev velocity some teams like JIT.
[03:05] Emily Carter: We can do either. Our recommendation for regulated apps is pre-provisioning with SCIM and SCIM delta syncs, and to limit JIT to non-privileged roles.
[03:18] Priya Patel: Also need SSO session timeout settings and re-auth intervals exposed so we can align to our SSO policy (max 12 hours for persistent sessions).
[03:30] Marco Singh: Session lifetime is configurable via the console or API. We can set forced reauth windows and rules for admin elevation requiring MFA.
[03:40] Tom Reyes: Speaking of MFA, can Redwood enforce step-up auth on sensitive operations?
[03:47] Marco Singh: Yes, you can require step-up MFA for admin-level APIs and for token issuance that grants elevated scopes.
[03:55] Aisha Khan: About encryption — we need server-side encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK) in our EU KMS. Does Redwood support external KMS/HSM?
[04:05] Marco Singh: We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed keys for on-prem/private deployments. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with your CMK; for Private deployment you can use an in-vpc HSM.
[04:20] Jared Lin: If we use CMK, does Redwood manage key rotation or do we?
[04:26] Marco Singh: Keys are managed by you in your KMS; Redwood uses them for envelope encryption. Rotation is handled per your KMS policies. We can coordinate with your security team on rotation windows.
[04:38] Emily Carter: Data residency — Nova said EU only for PII. We can pin customer data and logs to eu regions and prevent cross-region replication for those resources.
[04:50] Aisha Khan: We'll need an attestation that tokens and caches don't leave region. Also how do you handle KV cache if using multi-region serving?
[05:03] Marco Singh: We can configure model serving to use region-local caches. For multi-region failover we have routing policies that fall back only to designated regions; but for strict residency you can opt out of cross-region fallback. We'll document the control plane interactions.
[05:20] Tom Reyes: Ok, can we map example roles now? Say: platform-reader, platform-operator, platform-admin, security-auditor. platform-operator can deploy but not change billing, platform-admin can change deploy and billing.
[05:35] Marco Singh: Yes. For least-privilege we recommend that deploy pipelines use service accounts with scoped tokens and no UI access; human roles have UI permissions. We'll send a role matrix XLSX.
[05:50] Aisha Khan: On SCIM delta sync frequency — what is typical? We need near-real time provisioning for onboarding/offboarding.
[05:58] Marco Singh: SCIM delta sync is configurable; default every 5 minutes for high sync tiers, or you can trigger on-demand sync via API. That supports near-real-time provisioning.
[06:12] Priya Patel: For SOC2 evidence, we need proof of provisioning flows during onboarding. Do you record SAML assertion payloads or just events?
[06:22] Marco Singh: We store redacted assertion metadata and full audit events; we don't persist raw credentials. We can export events for audit and include trace IDs that link assertions to provisioning actions.
[06:35] Emily Carter: Any blockers from Nova's side to move to a pilot?
[06:40] Aisha Khan: We'll need the SCIM template and an understanding of what attributes Redwood requires. Also a short runbook for the SSO metadata exchange and tests to validate SAML response mapping.
[06:52] Emily Carter: We'll send the template and runbook. We'll also attach a checklist for auditors.
[06:58] Tom Reyes: One more — if we do a Dedicated deployment later, will roles and RBAC translate or is that a different control plane?
[07:07] Marco Singh: The same RBAC model and API are used across Hosted and Dedicated; Dedicated gives you isolated capacity but the semantic of roles is preserved. On Private there are extra synchronization options.
[07:20] Aisha Khan: About provisioning logs — can we stream SCIM logs to our SIEM in real-time?
[07:27] Marco Singh: Yes, via webhook, Kafka, or direct Cloud Storage export. We'll include recommended schema for SIEM ingestion.
[07:38] Jared Lin: For incident response, how fast can you rotate tokens or revoke sessions?
[07:44] Marco Singh: Immediate revocation via API; sessions accept a revocation event and are invalidated within seconds for interactive sessions and immediately for API tokens depending on TTL.
[07:56] Priya Patel: We also need role attestation every 90 days to meet internal policy. Can Redwood produce a periodic report of active privileged accounts?
[08:05] Marco Singh: Yes, you can schedule periodic exports of privileged role membership and last activity. That can feed into your attestation process.
[08:18] Emily Carter: Let's recap next steps and owners — I'll pull those together. Anything else?
[08:24] Tom Reyes: One small ask — sample SAML assertions with the attribute names you accept (e.g., email, uid, groups) would help our IdP config.
[08:35] Emily Carter: We'll add that to the runbook.
[08:38] Aisha Khan: Great. Thanks all.
[08:40] Emily Carter: Thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts and a calendar invite for the staging pilot.
[08:45] Marco Singh: I'll attach a short security FAQ and the role matrix.
[08:50] Meeting end.
